children: As many as 1.01 crore shares of Schaeffler India Ltd., changed hands in the pre-open block window on Thursday, November 26, according to available data on the exchanges. The stock is up 4% in early trade on Thursday.

The number of shares that changed hands amount to 6.5% of the company's outstanding equity. Shares changed hands at an average price of ₹3,493 apiece, taking the total transaction value to ₹3,543 crore.
CNBC-TV18 had reported on Wednesday that company's parent Schaeffler plans on selling up to 6% of their outstanding holdings through the block deal.
The floor price of ₹3,400 was a 5.6% discount to Wednesday's closing. Buyers and sellers are officially not known.
At the end of the September quarter, promoters of Schaeffler India had a 74.13% stake in the company, according to the BSE shareholding pattern, while the rest belonged to public shareholders.

Among the public shareholding, Mutual Funds own 15.1% stake, with Kotak, SBI, DSP, Axis and Nippon, owning stakes in the company. Foreign Portfolio Investors had a 4.29% stake in the company, while nearly 65,000 retail shareholders, or those with authorized share capital of up to ₹2 lakh, had a 3.7% stake in the company as of September 30.

Schaeffler India had announced alongside their second quarter results last month that its promoters may consider monetizing a part of their stake in the near future. They did go on to maintain that the promoters intend to keep control of the company, by owning at least two-thirds of the company's equity.
In case the promoters are indeed the sellers in this transaction, their overall shareholding will fall to around 67.6%.
Shares of Schaeffler India had ended 0.4% lower on Wednesday at ₹3,595. The stock is down 7.1% so far this year.

title: Schaeffler India shares gain up to 4% after ₹3,543 crore block deal, in-line with promoter plans
